headline: Coarse-grained models link crowding and protein charge to mRNA and nucleoid organization
label: Multiscale Simulation Of Macromolecular Assemblies
summary: Multiscale simulations now resolve how crowding and protein charge govern mRNA and nucleoid organization in cells.
synthesis: The common thread is coarse-graining of macromolecular structures to reach length and time scales inaccessible to all-atom simulation, applied to the spatial organization of crowded cellular components. A Kremer-Grest bead-spring molecular dynamics study reports that ribosome crowding on polysomes shifts the mRNA scaling exponent toward quasi-2D conformations. The JCVI-Syn3A coarse-grained model attributes the expanded nucleoid and ribosome distribution to abundant positively charged proteins that screen ribosome-DNA repulsion. ioNERDSS, a Python package, converts 3D atomic structures into coarse-grained models for rule-based stochastic self-assembly simulation. What is new is the explicit coupling of structure-derived coarse-grained representations to cell-scale and polysomal organization, with the Syn3A study as the only published item and the other two preprints.
